newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Winterthur sees continued earnings growth.
newsitem.headline: Winterthur sees continued earnings growth.

text.p: Insurance group HIH Winterthur International Holdings Ltd said on Friday it expected continued growth in core earnings in calendar 1997.
"The earnings outlook for 1997 is encouraging with continued growth in core earnings readily achievable," chairman Geoffrey Cohen told the annual meeting.
"Subject to movemenys in investment markets, this healthy position will carry through to after tax profits," Cohen said.
HIH Witherthur is about 48 percent owned by Winterthur Swiss Insurance Company.

"Although Australian general insurance markets remain soft overall, our selective business approach will enable us both to maintain aggregate premium levels and to register substantial organic growth through, for example, our financial institutions portfolio," Cohen said.

He said the company also expected further expansion in its United Kingdom and New Zealand operations and an immediate earnings contribution from its re-entry into the United States market in January with the US$59 million purchase of Care America Compensation and Liability Insurance Co.

"This acquisition provides a very neat strategic fit. In one move we have both established a regional hub for our businesses in the Americas while also acquiring the capacity to tap into those United States workers compensation markets where we can readily profit from our expertise."

Cohen said the company's activities in China and Argentina should be viewed as investments in the future with no plan for immediate returns. "Both regions offer vast potential and we want to be in a position to capitalise on opportunities as they arise rather than to join a long queue of aspiring insurers at some future date."
The company also remained on the lookout for further large and small acquisitions where there was a strategic fit and where the takeover price did not include excessive goodwil.
HIH achieved a 28 percent rise in calendar 1996 net profit to A$48.2 million and a 46 percent rise in net earned premium to A$931.4 million.
